title: The flaring drill in the Galactic centre. Did the IRS 13 cluster carve out the mini-cavity in the mini-spiral?
comment: To be published in Astronomy & Astrophysics; 5 pages, 2 figures
summary: The mini-cavity is a low-density region observed in the complex of streams of ionized gas around the Galactic central supermassive black hole, Sgr A$^\star$, known as the mini-spiral. Its near-circular shape is suggestive of a formation due to the effect of stellar winds. No suitable stars are currently observed within the mini-cavity, however. In this study we assessed whether the mini-cavity could have been formed by the winds of the stars from the neighbouring IRS 13 cluster that were located at the position of the mini-cavity in the past but moved away from it later on owing to their orbital motions around Sgr A$^\star$. Furthermore, we estimated the rate of accretion of the then-abundant interstellar medium onto the putative intermediate-mass black hole that has been proposed to reside in the IRS 13 cluster and the corresponding X-ray luminosity of this black hole. The estimates were obtained analytically using the astrophysical properties reported for the involved objects and the environment. Based on our results, we suggest that the mini-cavity was formed by the winds of the IRS 13 cluster member stars about 300 years ago, when this cluster went through the Bar region of the mini-spiral. The accompanying accretion of the interstellar medium onto the putative intermediate-mass black hole in this cluster may have produced multiple X-ray flares with luminosities of $\approx10^{39}$ erg/s. Such flares are compatible with the X-ray reflections currently observed on the molecular clouds in the complexes Sgr A, B, and C, including the necessary light-travel time delay.

AI.tldr: The mini-cavity in the Galactic center's mini-spiral was likely formed ~300 years ago by stellar winds from the IRS 13 cluster stars passing through the Bar region. Accretion onto a putative intermediate-mass black hole in IRS 13 could have produced X-ray flares (~10³⁹ erg/s) consistent with observed X-ray reflections in nearby molecular clouds.
AI.motivation: To explain the origin of the mini-cavity's near-circular shape in the mini-spiral around Sgr A*, given that no suitable stars currently reside within it to produce the necessary stellar winds.
AI.method: Analytical modeling using reported astrophysical properties of the IRS 13 cluster, the mini-spiral environment, and orbital dynamics around Sgr A* to estimate past positions, wind effects, accretion rates, and X-ray luminosities.
AI.result: The IRS 13 cluster passed through the Bar region ~300 years ago, and its stellar winds could have carved the mini-cavity. Accretion onto the putative intermediate-mass black hole could produce X-ray flares of ~10³⁹ erg/s, matching observed X-ray reflections in Sgr A, B, and C molecular clouds with appropriate light-travel time delays.
AI.conclusion: The mini-cavity was formed by IRS 13 cluster stellar winds ~300 years ago, and the accompanying IMBH accretion flares are viable progenitors for the X-ray reflections observed today in the Galactic center molecular cloud complexes.

title: Chemical enrichment of the Perseus cluster core seen by XRISM/Resolve
comment: 16 pages, 10 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: The intracluster medium (ICM) is rich in chemical elements, produced by core-collapse (SNIcc) and Type Ia supernovae (SNIa) over the last $\sim$12 Gyr. Whereas cluster outskirts are uniformly enriched with Fe at $\sim$0.3 solar - strongly suggesting that the gas had been pre-enriched during or before the assembly of galaxies into clusters, the Fe abundance is known to centrally increase in the core of relaxed clusters. The origin of these central Fe peaks however, as well as the apparent presence of mysterious drops previously reported in the very centre of a number of systems, remain to be clarified. In this paper, we address these two questions by measuring the spatial distribution of Fe and its relative Si/Fe, S/Fe, Ar/Fe, Ca/Fe, Cr/Fe, Mn/Fe, and Ni/Fe ratios in the X-ray bright, nearby Perseus cluster. We take advantage of the unprecedented spectral resolution ($\sim$5 eV) offered by the Resolve microcalorimeter on board XRISM, which observed four distinct pointings of Perseus out to $\sim$250 kpc ($\sim$0.2$r_{500}$) during its Performance Verification phase. Although the presence of an X-ray bright AGN challenges a precise quantification of absolute abundances in the very core, our baseline analysis rules out a strong drop with $>$2$σ$ confidence, at variance with previous CCD measurements. In addition, we find a remarkable spatial uniformity of X/Fe ratios, supporting the idea of negligible late SNIa enrichment from the brightest cluster galaxy NGC 1275. We also compare the overall chemical composition of the Perseus ICM with SNcc and SNIa nucleosynthesis yield models, finding that the co-existence of two separate SNIa enrichment channels is not needed to reproduce the ICM ratios satisfactorily.

AI.tldr: Using XRISM/Resolve data, we find no significant central Fe drop in the Perseus cluster (contradicting earlier CCD results), and show that X/Fe ratios are spatially uniform, indicating negligible late SNIa enrichment from NGC 1275; a single SNIa channel suffices to explain the observed ICM composition.
AI.motivation: To clarify the origin of central Fe abundance peaks in relaxed clusters and investigate previously reported mysterious central Fe drops, using high-resolution XRISM observations of the Perseus cluster.
AI.method: Measured spatial distributions of Fe and X/Fe ratios (Si, S, Ar, Ca, Cr, Mn, Ni) in the Perseus ICM out to ~250 kpc using XRISM/Resolve microcalorimeter data (~5 eV resolution) across four pointings, and compared with SNcc and SNIa nucleosynthesis yield models.
AI.result: No significant central Fe drop is detected (>2σ confidence, contrary to previous CCD results). X/Fe ratios show remarkable spatial uniformity, challenging the need for late SNIa enrichment from NGC 1275. A single SNIa enrichment channel can reproduce the observed ICM ratios.
AI.conclusion: The central Fe peak in Perseus is not accompanied by a central drop; the uniform X/Fe ratios imply limited late-time SNIa contribution from the central galaxy; a single SNIa channel is sufficient to explain the ICM chemical composition.

title: Decoupled Kinematics and Excitation in the Compton-thick AGN NGC 6552: Spatially Resolved KOOLS-IFU Observations
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: Hard X-ray selected Compton-thick AGNs provide a relatively obscuration-resistant census of accretion, but optical line diagnostics can be strongly shaped by extinction and geometry. Spatially resolved integral-field spectroscopy can mitigate these effects and provides direct constraints on outflow kinematics and ionization state on kiloparsec scales. We present KOOLS-IFU optical integral-field spectroscopy of NGC 6552 obtained on the 3.8 m Seimei Telescope. Using spatially resolved emission-line ratios and non-parametric [O III]5007 kinematics over the central ~2 kpc, we test whether ionized-gas kinematics are locally coupled to excitation. The [O III]5007 width W80 is broadly elevated across the inner region (~530-830 km/s) and declines monotonically with projected galactocentric distance, consistent with a centrally concentrated outflow that decelerates at larger radii. Despite this clear kinematic structure, neither W80 nor the velocity asymmetry parameter dv shows a statistically significant correlation with [O III]5007/Hbeta. Order-of-magnitude outflow energetics yield Edot_K/L_bol ~ 0.01%-0.28% (for assumed n_e = 50-1000 cm^-3), consistent with [O III]-based estimates tracing only the ionized phase of a multi-phase outflow. We conclude that in NGC 6552 both the total line broadening traced by W80 and dv are consistent with being governed primarily by spatial dynamical structure and line-of-sight superposition of multiple kinematic components, with no statistically significant coupling to excitation-driven processes detected at our sensitivity level. A positive W80-[O III]5007/Hbeta coupling does emerge in the small subset of bins for which the two-component fit is most strongly favored statistically, which deeper observations will be needed to confirm.

AI.tldr: This paper presents KOOLS-IFU optical integral-field spectroscopy of the Compton-thick AGN NGC 6552. The study finds that [O III]5007 line width W80 declines radially, consistent with a decelerating outflow, but shows no statistically significant correlation with [O III]5007/Hβ, suggesting line broadening is governed by spatial dynamics and line-of-sight kinematic superposition rather than local excitation. A weak positive coupling emerges only in a small subset of bins where two-component fitting is preferred.
AI.motivation: To test whether ionized-gas kinematics are locally coupled to excitation in the Compton-thick AGN NGC 6552 using spatially resolved integral-field spectroscopy, mitigating obscuration and extinction effects that plague traditional optical diagnostics.
AI.method: KOOLS-IFU optical integral-field spectroscopy on the 3.8 m Seimei Telescope; spatially resolved emission-line ratio mapping; non-parametric [O III]5007 kinematics (W80, dv) over ~2 kpc central region; two-component line profile fitting.
AI.result: W80 is elevated (530-830 km/s) and declines radially, but shows no statistically significant correlation with [O III]5007/Hβ. Outflow energetics yield Ė_K/L_bol ~ 0.01%-0.28% (n_e=50-1000 cm⁻³). A positive W80–[O III]5007/Hβ coupling is only seen in a small subset where two-component fits are statistically favored.
AI.conclusion: In NGC 6552, ionized-gas kinematics are primarily governed by spatial dynamical structure and line-of-sight superposition of kinematic components, not local excitation processes. Deeper observations are needed to confirm any weak excitation–kinematics coupling.

title: MEGA and SMILES Find Fewer Dusty Galaxies than Expected at Cosmic Noon
comment: 15 pages, 8 figues, 5 tables,
summary: We present infrared (IR) luminsosity functions (LFs) and resulting star formation rate densities using the JWST Mid-infrared Instrument (MIRI) observations from the MIRI EGS Galaxy and AGN (MEGA) survey and Systematic MIRI Legacy Extragalactic Survey (SMILES). JWST allows us to perform a robust analysis on the faint end of the IR LF beyond the local universe. We directly measure the 7.7$μ$m polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon (PAH) feature using either F1000W, F1500W, or F2100W photometry. This results in a sample of 634 galaxies across the two surveys covering an area of 105 arcmin$^2$ ($\sim$70 in the EGS and $\sim35$ in the GOODS-S/HUDF fields) and spanning $0.2<z<2$. We convert the 7.7$μ$m PAH luminosity to total IR luminosity, resulting in LFs that are two orders of magnitude fainter than previous studies. In contrast to previous extrapolations based on shallower observations, we find a strong flattening in the faint end of the LF with an average slope of $α\sim0.147$. This indicates that less luminous galaxies do not have as much dust obscured star formation as predicted. We measure the star formation rate density (SFRD) by integrating our new IR LFs and find a slightly lower SFRD in all redshift bins than previous studies made with ALMA, Herschel, and Spitzer. We also measure the contribution to the SFRD as a function of luminosity and confirm that LIRGs and ULIRGs remain the dominant contributors to the dust-obscured star formation at $z\sim1-2$.

AI.tldr: Using JWST MIRI observations from MEGA and SMILES surveys, the paper presents IR luminosity functions and star formation rate densities for 634 galaxies at 0.2<z<2, finding a flattening in the faint-end LF slope (α~0.147), two orders of magnitude fainter than previous studies, and slightly lower SFRD than ALMA/Herschel/Spitzer measurements.
AI.motivation: To robustly analyze the faint end of the infrared luminosity function beyond the local universe using JWST MIRI's superior sensitivity, challenging previous extrapolations based on shallower observations.
AI.method: Used JWST MIRI photometry (F1000W, F1500W, F2100W) to directly measure the 7.7μm PAH feature for 634 galaxies from MEGA and SMILES surveys (105 arcmin² total area), converted PAH luminosity to total IR luminosity to construct LFs down to two orders of magnitude fainter than prior work.
AI.result: Found a strong flattening in the faint-end LF slope (α~0.147), indicating less dust-obscured star formation in low-luminosity galaxies than previously predicted; measured slightly lower SFRD across all redshift bins compared to ALMA, Herschel, and Spitzer; confirmed LIRGs and ULIRGs as dominant contributors to dust-obscured star formation at z~1-2.
AI.conclusion: JWST reveals that faint galaxies have less dust-obscured star formation than earlier shallower surveys suggested, revising downward the SFRD estimates and confirming the dominant role of luminous IR galaxies at cosmic noon.

title: Hawai`i Supernova Flows: Bulk Flow Measurements using SNe Ia in the Optical and NIR
comment: 20 pages, 7 figures. All code available at https://github.com/ado8/hsf_bulkflows
summary: The present day peculiar velocity-field was sourced by primordial density fluctuations and sculpted over the lifespan of the Universe. Cosmological models such as $Λ$CDM make predictions for various statistical properties of peculiar velocities. Bulk flow, the average velocity within a given volume, has an expectation value of $\vec{0}$ due to isotropy, and a variance directly tied to the Hubble constant, the growth-rate of structure, and the matter power spectrum. In this paper, we use the redshifts and optical and near-infrared distance estimates to Type Ia Supernovae (SNe Ia) within subsets of the Hawai`i Supernova Flows dataset to infer the bulk flow within $z \lesssim 0.1$. The inferred speeds vary between ~100 to 400 km/s but are all consistent with the predictions of $Λ$CDM. As a secondary focus, we discuss the systematic uncertainty introduced by the discrete choice of methodology using two bulk flow estimators, two types of SN Ia distance estimators, and data covering two distinct regimes in wavelength space.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the peculiar velocity field using Type Ia Supernovae data to infer bulk flows within z ≲ 0.1, finding speeds of ~100-400 km/s consistent with ΛCDM predictions, while also examining systematic uncertainties from different methodological choices.
AI.motivation: To understand how primordial density fluctuations shaped the present-day peculiar velocity field and to test ΛCDM model predictions by measuring bulk flows using SN Ia data.
AI.method: The authors use redshifts and optical/near-infrared distance estimates to Type Ia Supernovae from the Hawai`i Supernova Flows dataset, employing two bulk flow estimators, two types of SN Ia distance estimators, and data covering two wavelength regimes to infer the bulk flow within z ≲ 0.1.
AI.result: Inferred bulk flow speeds vary between ~100 to 400 km/s, all consistent with ΛCDM model predictions.
AI.conclusion: The peculiar velocity measurements are consistent with ΛCDM cosmology, and the choice of methodology introduces systematic uncertainty that should be carefully considered.

title: Hector Galaxy Survey: Optical IFU and Chandra Reveal a Low-Luminosity AGN Behind Extended LINER Emission
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ
summary: We present evidence that the Hector Galaxy Survey galaxy C901005481609968 ($z_{\rm cl}=0.0553$), which exhibits spatially extended LINER-like emission in optical integral-field spectroscopy (IFS), hosts a low-luminosity active galactic nucleus (LLAGN) that contributes substantially to its ionization budget. Although the galaxy is not selected as an AGN by mid-infrared AGN color criteria, archival Chandra data reveal a compact nuclear X-ray source with $\log L_{\rm X}\approx41.46$ erg/s, supporting the presence of an LLAGN. Spatially resolved emission-line diagnostics show LINER-like line ratios across most spaxels with $\mathrm{S/N} \geq 3$, while spatially resolved $τ$ maps ($τ\equiv Q_{\rm pAGB}/Q_{\rm req}$) indicate a widespread photon deficit ($\logτ<0$ over most of the mapped region), even under the most optimistic pAGB normalizations, the nuclear region remains at $τ< 1$. Line-ratio--kinematic tests find no evidence for shock-dominated excitation as the primary driver of the extended emission, although a localized or sub-dominant shock contribution cannot be ruled out with the present data. We use this galaxy as a pilot case because the combination of Hector IFS and an independent nuclear X-ray constraint provides a stringent validation of the spatially resolved photon-budget framework. Our results indicate that evolved stellar populations alone cannot account for the observed emission, that an additional nuclear ionizing source is required at least in the inner region, and that a weak LLAGN likely contributes to the ionizing budget, particularly in the inner region. Our results demonstrate that extended LINER-like emission can conceal a substantial LLAGN contribution even when traditional optical and infrared AGN indicators are weak, and that spatially resolved photon-budget tests combined with X-ray constraints can effectively reveal such hidden activity.

AI.tldr: A galaxy (C901005481609968) with extended LINER-like emission hosts a low-luminosity AGN (LLAGN) not detected by mid-infrared AGN selection; spatially resolved photon-budget and X-ray analyses show evolved stars alone cannot account for the ionization, revealing a hidden LLAGN contribution.
AI.motivation: To test whether extended LINER-like emission in IFS can be fully explained by evolved stellar populations (pAGB stars) or if an additional LLAGN source is required, using a galaxy with both Hector IFS and independent X-ray constraints as a pilot case.
AI.method: Combined Hector IFS (optical emission-line diagnostics), archival Chandra X-ray data (nuclear compact source detection), spatially resolved τ maps (τ = Q_pAGB / Q_req) to quantify photon deficits, line-ratio–kinematic tests to check shock contribution, and mid-infrared AGN color criteria for comparison.
AI.result: Chandra reveals a compact nuclear X-ray source (log L_X ≈ 41.46 erg/s); LINER-like ratios across most spaxels; widespread photon deficit (log τ < 0) even under optimistic pAGB normalizations, with τ < 1 in the nuclear region; no evidence for shock-dominated excitation as primary driver.
AI.conclusion: Extended LINER-like emission can conceal a substantial LLAGN contribution when traditional optical/IR AGN indicators are weak; spatially resolved photon-budget tests combined with X-ray constraints effectively reveal such hidden AGN activity.

title: Tracing Ultra Light Axions in Post-reionization, Lyman-$α$ and CMB Missions
comment: 12 sets of figures. 2 tables. Comments are welcome!
summary: Ultra-light axions (ULAs) are dark matter candidates proposed to resolve the small scale anomalies of the standard cosmological model. Due to their inherent quantum pressure, ULAs result in a distinct, scale-dependent suppression on the matter power spectrum, which can leave imprints on the upcoming observations. We explore such possibilities by forecasting on the post-reionization large scale structure (LSS) surveys and next-generation cosmic microwave background (CMB) missions. By utilizing the cross-correlation between 21-cm intensity mapping (SKA1-MID and PUMA) and the Lyman-$α$ forest (DESI-like), we explore possible signatures of ULAs in post-reionization surveys while mitigating instrument-specific systematics. The Fisher matrix analysis projects uncertainties on the fractional ULA abundance across a wide ULA mass range of $10^{-30}\text{ eV} \le m_a \le 10^{-20}\text{ eV}$, revealing an optimal detection sensitivity at intermediate masses around $m_a \sim 10^{-25}\text{ eV}$. Furthermore, while next-generation CMB mission alone can yield small projected errors on the ULA fraction compared to future LSS missions, a joint analysis of the DESI-like and PUMA cross-spectrum alongside CMB-S4-like missions estimates an error on the ULA fraction to be $\mathcal{O}(10^{-4})$ for $m_a\lesssim 10^{-28}$ eV, highlighting a significant improvement over standalone LSS and CMB missions.

AI.tldr: The paper forecasts detectability of ultra-light axion (ULA) dark matter using cross-correlation of 21-cm intensity mapping and Lyman-α forest surveys, combined with CMB data, finding optimal sensitivity at m_a ~ 10^{-25} eV and joint errors of O(10^{-4}) for m_a ≲ 10^{-28} eV.
AI.motivation: ULAs are proposed to resolve small-scale anomalies of ΛCDM, and their quantum pressure induces scale-dependent suppression on the matter power spectrum that may be detectable in upcoming surveys.
AI.method: Fisher matrix forecasting using cross-correlation between 21-cm intensity mapping (SKA1-MID, PUMA) and Lyman-α forest (DESI-like) to probe ULA signatures in post-reionization LSS, alongside next-generation CMB missions (CMB-S4-like).
AI.result: Optimal detection sensitivity at intermediate masses m_a ~ 10^{-25} eV; joint DESI-like + PUMA + CMB-S4 analysis yields O(10^{-4}) error on ULA fraction for m_a ≲ 10^{-28} eV, significantly improving over standalone missions.
AI.conclusion: Cross-correlating 21-cm and Lyman-α forest surveys with CMB data provides powerful constraints on ULA dark matter across a wide mass range (10^{-30}–10^{-20} eV).

title: Chemical hints of Population III stars from silicon abundances in massive galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in A&A; 15 pages, 7 figures, 2 tables
summary: The formation of massive galaxies remains a fundamental question in astrophysics, with recent JWST observations suggesting that intense star formation occurred earlier than previously expected. We used the prototypical massive relic galaxy NGC 1277 as a fossil record to probe the chemical signatures of early star formation. With a stellar mass of $1.2 \pm 0.4 \times 10^{11}M_\odot$ and a compact structure (half-light radius of 1.2 kpc), NGC 1277 is representative of massive relic galaxies-systems that formed rapidly at high redshifts ("red nuggets" at $z>2$) and have since undergone largely passive evolution, preserving the imprint of their earliest stellar populations. Using deep near-infrared spectroscopy, we identified unusually strong silicon (Si) absorption features in this galaxy. We measure $[\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{Fe}]=1.05^{+0.45}_{-0.27}$ and $[\mathrm{Mg}/\mathrm{Fe}]=0.36^{+0.27}_{-0.24}$, corresponding to a significantly enhanced silicon-to-magnesium ratio ($[\mathrm{Si}/\mathrm{Mg}]=0.67^{+0.45}_{-0.27}$) which cannot be reproduced by current stellar population models or typical core-collapse supernova yields. This enhancement suggests a contribution from very massive, metal-poor progenitors during the earliest phases of star formation. Such conditions are consistent with nucleosynthetic yields from pair-instability supernovae or other enrichment channels associated with extremely massive stars, whose chemical signatures are expected to remain less diluted in systems like NGC 1277 due to their rapid formation timescales and minimal late-time accretion. This result provides rare chemical evidence of early massive-star enrichment preserved in a local relic galaxy and opens a new observational window into the chemical evolution of the Universe.

AI.tldr: JWST-motivated study of the massive relic galaxy NGC 1277 reveals unusually enhanced silicon absorption features ([Si/Mg]=0.67), indicating contributions from very massive, metal-poor progenitor stars (e.g., pair-instability supernovae) during early, rapid star formation, preserved due to the galaxy's passive evolution since high redshift.
AI.motivation: To understand early massive galaxy formation using local relic galaxies as fossil records, motivated by JWST discoveries of unexpectedly early intense star formation.
AI.method: Deep near-infrared spectroscopy of NGC 1277 to measure elemental abundances (Si, Mg, Fe), comparing observed chemical signatures against stellar population models and supernova yield predictions.
AI.result: Detected strongly enhanced silicon absorption features: [Si/Fe]=1.05, [Mg/Fe]=0.36, yielding [Si/Mg]=0.67 — ratios that cannot be reproduced by current stellar population models or standard core-collapse supernova yields.
AI.conclusion: The unusual Si enhancement provides rare chemical evidence of early massive-star enrichment (likely pair-instability supernovae) preserved in a local relic galaxy, opening a new observational window into early chemical evolution.

title: Damped Harmonic Oscillator Dark Energy and the Hubble Tension
comment: 9 pages, 5 figures, All comments are welcome
summary: We investigate a dark-energy equation of state governed by a damped harmonic oscillator equation, admitting underdamped, critically damped, and overdamped solutions. Confronting the model against Planck CMB, DESI BAO, BBN, Cosmic Chronometers, and three Type~Ia supernova compilations, we find that the underdamped solution yields $H_0 = 70.9 \pm 1.1$ km/s/Mpc, with DESY5 and $H_0 = 72.0^{+1.4}_{-2.1}$ km/s/Mpc with Union3, reducing the tension with SH0ES to $\sim\!1.4σ$, while Pantheon+ strongly favors a near-critically damped solution with positive $w_0$ and $H_0 = 66.23 \pm 0.85$ km/s/Mpc, revealing a significant systematic tension among supernova datasets. Bayesian evidence relative to $Λ$CDM is inconclusive for DES and Union3 data, demonstrating that $H_0$ tension alleviation is achievable at no statistical cost relative to the standard model.

AI.tldr: A dark-energy model governed by a damped harmonic oscillator equation is tested against multiple cosmological datasets. The underdamped solution can reduce the H₀ tension with SH0ES to ~1.4σ, while Pantheon+ favors a near-critically damped solution with positive w₀. Bayesian evidence shows no statistical penalty relative to ΛCDM.
AI.motivation: To explore whether a dark-energy equation of state following a damped harmonic oscillator dynamics can alleviate the H₀ tension between early- and late-universe measurements.
AI.method: The authors model dark energy via a damped harmonic oscillator equation (underdamped, critically damped, overdamped regimes) and fit the model to combined datasets: Planck CMB, DESI BAO, BBN, Cosmic Chronometers, and three Type Ia supernova compilations (DESY5, Union3, Pantheon+). Bayesian model comparison against ΛCDM is performed.
AI.result: Underdamped solution yields H₀ = 70.9 ± 1.1 km/s/Mpc (DESY5) and H₀ = 72.0⁺¹.⁴₋₂.₁ km/s/Mpc (Union3), reducing tension with SH0ES to ~1.4σ. Pantheon+ favors a near-critically damped solution with positive w₀ and H₀ = 66.23 ± 0.85 km/s/Mpc, indicating systematic tension among SN datasets. Bayesian evidence relative to ΛCDM is inconclusive for DES and Union3.
AI.conclusion: H₀ tension alleviation is achievable at no statistical cost relative to ΛCDM, but systematic differences among supernova datasets significantly impact inferred cosmological parameters.

title: Exploring the Relationship Between Bars, Star Formation Activity, and Host Galaxy Properties from $\mathbf{z \sim 0}$ to $\mathbf{z \sim 2}$
comment: 29 pages, 17 figures. Submitted to ApJ
summary: We present the most comprehensive study to date of the relationship between bars, star formation, and galaxy properties from $z \sim$ 0 to $z \sim$ 2. We use a mass-complete sample of 1,171 galaxies from the JWST CEERS survey with $M_\star > 10^{10} M_\odot$ and repeat the analysis using COSMOS-Web data. Our results are: 1) At high redshift ($z \sim$ $1-2$) barred galaxies tend to have high sSFRs and low Sérsic indices ($n \leq 2$), while at low redshifts barred galaxies emerge with both low sSFR and higher $n$, suggestive of quiescent galaxies with bulges. 2) The fractional contribution of barred quiescent galaxies to the bar fraction rises steeply from $z \sim$ 2 to $z \sim$ 0, while that of barred actively star-forming galaxies falls. 3) The fraction of quiescent galaxies that are barred rises steeply over the last 10 Gyr. 4) Our empirical results show good agreement with the TNG50-1 simulations for bars with $a_{\mathrm{bar}}$ $>$ 1.5 kpc. Our results allow for the possibility that bar-driven secular evolution may lead to quiescence and/or that bars are more likely to persist and grow in gas-poor, quiescent galaxies. The steep rise in the quiescent bar fraction over 10 Gyr may represent an evolutionary sequence whereby gas-rich disks at high redshift first develop short, dynamically young bars and over time, repeated bar-driven gas inflows lead to central starbursts and declining gas fractions that strengthen the bar as the galaxy transitions toward quiescence.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes 1,171 galaxies from JWST CEERS and COSMOS-Web surveys to examine the relationship between bars, star formation, and galaxy properties from z~0 to z~2. At high redshift (z~1-2), barred galaxies have high sSFR and low Sérsic indices (n≤2); at low redshift, barred galaxies have low sSFR and higher n. The fraction of barred quiescent galaxies rises steeply over 10 Gyr while barred star-forming galaxies decline. Results agree with TNG50-1 simulations and suggest bar-driven secular evolution may lead to quiescence.
AI.motivation: To provide the most comprehensive study to date of the relationship between bars, star formation, and galaxy properties across cosmic time from z~0 to z~2 using high-quality JWST data.
AI.method: Used a mass-complete sample of 1,171 galaxies from JWST CEERS survey with M⋆ > 10¹⁰ M⊙ and repeated the analysis using COSMOS-Web data. Compared empirical results with TNG50-1 simulations for bars with a_bar > 1.5 kpc.
AI.result: 1) At high redshift (z~1-2), barred galaxies have high sSFR and low Sérsic indices (n≤2); at low redshift, barred galaxies have low sSFR and higher n. 2) Barred quiescent galaxies' fractional contribution to bar fraction rises steeply from z~2 to z~0, while barred star-forming galaxies' contribution falls. 3) Quiescent galaxy bar fraction rises steeply over last 10 Gyr. 4) Good agreement with TNG50-1 simulations for bars >1.5 kpc.
AI.conclusion: Bar-driven secular evolution may lead to quiescence, and/or bars are more likely to persist and grow in gas-poor, quiescent galaxies. The steep rise in quiescent bar fraction over 10 Gyr suggests an evolutionary sequence where gas-rich disks develop short, dynamically young bars, and repeated bar-driven gas inflows lead to central starbursts and declining gas fractions that strengthen the bar as the galaxy transitions toward quiescence.

title: Joint reconstruction of $H(z)$ and $fσ_8(z)$ with physics informed neural networks
comment: 22 pages; 7 figures
summary: We present a proof of concept for the joint reconstruction of the Hubble parameter $H(z)$ that assumes no dark energy equation of state and the growth rate of large scale structure $fσ_8(z)$ using a physics informed neural network. Rather than fitting these two observables separately and checking their consistency post hoc, we couple them through the linear growth equation of general relativity directly during training, using the equation residual evaluated at collocation points via automatic differentiation as an additional loss term. The network employs a shared backbone feeding two independent output heads, one per observable. We train an ensemble of 100 independently seeded networks on a compilation of 50 $H(z)$ measurements from Cosmic Chronometers and Baryon Acoustic Oscillations and 63 $fσ_8(z)$ measurements from Redshift Space Distortions, and study four values of the physics coupling weight $λ\in \{0,\,0.01,\,0.1,\,1.0\}$. We then anchor the $H_0$ normalization using two independent local distance scale determinations: the SH0ES result $H_0 = 73.04 \pm 1.04$\,km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$ and the Local Distance Network consensus $H_0 = 73.50 \pm 0.81$\,km\,s$^{-1}$\,Mpc$^{-1}$. With either prior the Hubble constant is recovered exactly at the prior value, and the two reconstructions are indistinguishable in $fσ_8(z)$. The reconstructed $fσ_8(z)$ sits systematically below the $Λ$CDM prediction at all redshifts, consistent with the $σ_8$ tension, while the $\mathrm{Om}(z)$ null test shows a marked departure from the flat $Λ$CDM expectation at low redshift. The results establish that coupling the two observables through the growth equation during training is both feasible and beneficial, and that the reconstruction is robust to the choice between the two local $H_0$ determinations.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a physics-informed neural network that jointly reconstructs the Hubble parameter H(z) and growth rate fσ₈(z) by coupling them through the linear growth equation of general relativity during training, using an ensemble of 100 networks on real observational data. Reconstructions using two local H₀ priors show that fσ₈(z) sits systematically below ΛCDM predictions (consistent with the σ₈ tension), and the Om(z) null test deviates from flat ΛCDM at low redshift.
AI.motivation: To jointly reconstruct H(z) and fσ₈(z) while enforcing physical consistency through the linear growth equation of general relativity, rather than fitting them separately and checking consistency post hoc.
AI.method: A physics-informed neural network with a shared backbone and two independent output heads is trained on 50 H(z) measurements (Cosmic Chronometers + BAO) and 63 fσ₈(z) measurements (RSD). The linear growth equation residual at collocation points (via automatic differentiation) serves as an additional physics loss term. An ensemble of 100 independently seeded networks is trained for four values of the physics coupling weight λ ∈ {0, 0.01, 0.1, 1.0}. Two local H₀ priors (SH0ES and Local Distance Network) anchor the normalization.
AI.result: With either H₀ prior, the Hubble constant is recovered exactly at the prior value, and the fσ₈(z) reconstructions are indistinguishable. The reconstructed fσ₈(z) sits systematically below the ΛCDM prediction at all redshifts, consistent with the σ₈ tension. The Om(z) null test shows a marked departure from flat ΛCDM expectation at low redshift.
AI.conclusion: Coupling H(z) and fσ₈(z) through the growth equation during training is both feasible and beneficial; the reconstruction is robust to the choice between the two local H₀ determinations.

title: Testing masking effectiveness using multi-line image cubes based on COSMOS2020 for [CII] line intensity mapping at $z_{[CII]} > 3.5$
comment: 23 pages, 22 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: We created line intensity mapping intensity cubes for CO and [CII] emission lines using the COSMOS2020 galaxy catalogue, forming predictions based on empirical data, for observations from Prime-Cam mounted on the Fred Young Submm Telescope. We also included simulated noise including white and correlated components, and tested masking techniques to recover [CII] signal at $3.5<z<8.2$. We applied line luminosity models to the COSMOS2020 galaxy catalogue, spanning 1.44deg$^2$, to estimate the [CII] and CO J=1-0 emission, with other CO transitions derived using Spectral Line Energy Distribution templates. From these we made cubes for four 40 GHz bands in the EoR-Spec frequency range (205-420GHz), as well as a potential future upgrade to EoR-Spec including bands at 150 and 90GHz. Given the incompleteness of the empirical catalogue, these predictions are conservative lower limits, which we subsequently extrapolated from. We applied masks to recover the [CII] power spectra, using bright galaxies of COSMOS2020 as a foreground catalogue to target CO at low z (targeted masking), and matching bright voxels across frequency bands to eliminate those associated with CO emission (blind masking). Our CO intensity cube predictions are consistent with ALMA, VLA and NOEMA observations, indicating that this method gives realistic CO estimates for E-COSMOS. In ideal conditions, masking can recover [CII] above 300GHz, with targeted masking requiring a complete foreground catalogue of bright CO sources to prevent them from contributing to contaminant emission, and blind masking needing additional lower frequency ranges to be effective. However, noise will hinder [CII] recovery above 300 GHz until near the end of the currently planned 2000 hour observing period, as $S/N<5$ without extra observing time. Whilst CO can be recovered below 300GHz, [CII] will be unavailable without cross correlation techniques.

AI.tldr: This study creates CO and [CII] line intensity mapping cubes using the COSMOS2020 galaxy catalogue for Prime-Cam on FYST, tests masking techniques to recover [CII] signal at 3.5<z<8.2, and finds that while CO can be recovered below 300 GHz, [CII] requires significant observing time (>2000 hours) for S/N>5 and remains unavailable without cross-correlation techniques.
AI.motivation: To generate realistic, empirical-data-based predictions for CO and [CII] line intensity mapping with Prime-Cam on FYST, and to evaluate masking techniques for recovering faint [CII] signal from bright foreground CO contamination across high-redshift ranges.
AI.method: Applied line luminosity models to the COSMOS2020 galaxy catalogue (1.44 deg²) to estimate [CII] and CO J=1-0 emission; derived higher CO transitions using SLED templates; constructed intensity cubes for four 40 GHz bands (205-420 GHz) plus future 90/150 GHz bands; added white and correlated noise; tested targeted masking (using bright COSMOS2020 galaxies as foreground catalogue) and blind masking (matching bright voxels across frequency bands) for [CII] power spectrum recovery.
AI.result: CO predictions are consistent with ALMA, VLA, and NOEMA observations; masking can recover [CII] above 300 GHz in ideal conditions but noise limits S/N<5 until near end of 2000-hour observing period; targeted masking requires complete foreground CO catalogue; blind masking needs additional lower-frequency bands; CO recoverable below 300 GHz but [CII] unavailable without cross-correlation.
AI.conclusion: The method produces realistic CO estimates for E-COSMOS; [CII] detection above 300 GHz is challenging even with masking, requiring substantial observing time; below 300 GHz, only CO is recoverable; cross-correlation techniques are necessary for [CII] at lower frequencies.

title: Synergy between CSST and future gravitational-wave detectors: Probing primordial black holes by cross-correlating dark sirens with galaxies
comment: 13 pages, 5 figures
summary: Gravitational-wave (GW) events and galaxies both trace the cosmic matter distribution, but the mergers of astrophysical black holes and primordial black holes (PBHs) are expected to populate different environments and therefore to cluster with different biases. The GW clustering bias is thus a statistical observable that can separate the two populations. We assess how well this can be done by cross-correlating the photometric galaxy survey of the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) with mock GW catalogs from two future detector networks: the third-generation ET2CE network (the Einstein Telescope and two Cosmic Explorer detectors) and the multi-band BDET2CE network, which adds the space-based baseline Decihertz Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory. We find that CSST combined with 10 years of ET2CE observations can reveal a PBH contribution once its fraction in the total merger rate exceeds about $40\%$, while the much sharper sky localization of BDET2CE lowers this threshold to about $20\%$. The improvement comes from recovering the small-scale clustering information that localization errors would otherwise erase. These results show that combining future GW detector networks with CSST galaxy clustering offers a promising and largely independent route to identifying PBHs statistically.

AI.tldr: This paper shows that cross-correlating future gravitational-wave (GW) events with CSST galaxy surveys can statistically separate primordial black holes (PBHs) from astrophysical black holes by measuring their clustering bias. With ET2CE (10 years), PBHs are detectable if they constitute >40% of mergers; adding the space-based BDET2CE improves localization and lowers the threshold to ~20%.
AI.motivation: To statistically distinguish primordial black holes (PBHs) from astrophysical black holes using their different clustering biases in the cosmic matter distribution, as PBHs and astrophysical BH mergers populate different environments.
AI.method: Cross-correlating mock GW catalogs (from ET2CE and BDET2CE detector networks) with photometric galaxy surveys from the Chinese Space-station Survey Telescope (CSST) and measuring the clustering bias as a statistical observable.
AI.result: CSST + 10 years ET2CE can detect PBH contribution when PBH fraction exceeds ~40%; BDET2CE's superior sky localization lowers this threshold to ~20% by preserving small-scale clustering information.
AI.conclusion: Combining future GW detector networks with CSST galaxy clustering provides a promising and largely independent statistical method for identifying PBHs.

title: Dust-Embedded Star Formation: Bridging Magellanic Cloud Studies of Massive Young Stellar Objects to Nearby Spiral Galaxies
comment: Accepted for publication in ApJ; 31 pages, 21 figures, 4 tables
summary: We use JWST NIRCam and MIRI imaging at 2, 4, 10, and 21 um to study young, dusty compact sources in four nearby galaxies at distances of ~ 1-5Mpc (M33, NGC300, NGC7793, and NGC5068). This work bridges well-characterized massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) in the Magellanic Clouds from the Spitzer SAGE survey to new studies of embedded clusters in more distant galaxies with JWST. Guided by the SAGE-LMC catalog, we define JWST color-magnitude selection criteria (F1000W versus F1000W-F2100W) and test them using resolution-degradation experiments. We identify 216, 32, 80 and 139 dusty young objects in the four galaxies, respectively. The selected population spans sources from systems dominated by a single MYSO to compact marginally resolved sources hosting multiple MYSOs. The color selection remains stable across 1-5 Mpc, and the 10um luminosity function retains a slope of alpha~ -2. However, blending and surface-brightness dilution remove fainter sources, leading to incompleteness of up to ~ 50% at 5.2 Mpc and biasing the sample toward brighter objects (F1000W < 19 mag). The sample spans approximate stellar masses of ~10-2 X 10^5 Mo. Spatial resolution affects the interpretation of mid-infrared emission: clustering increases the fraction of emission attributed to compact sources in active regions, while blending into diffuse emission dominates in quiescent environments. Comparisons with PAH-selected young clusters in the PHANGS galaxy NGC5068 show that our selection recovers ~ 80% of the PAH-selected sources. We show that the practical limit for studying individual MYSOs with JWST is ~3 Mpc. The resulting catalog provides a foundation for future resolved studies of star formation rates and early cluster evolution.

AI.tldr: This paper uses JWST NIRCam and MIRI imaging to study 467 dusty young compact sources in four nearby galaxies (M33, NGC300, NGC7793, NGC5068), establishing color-magnitude selection criteria at 10 and 21 μm inspired by Spitzer SAGE-LMC surveys. The selected population spans from single massive young stellar objects (MYSOs) to compact clusters, with a practical distance limit of ~3 Mpc for resolving individual MYSOs, and blending causing up to 50% incompleteness at 5.2 Mpc.
AI.motivation: To bridge the gap between well-characterized MYSOs in the Magellanic Clouds (Spitzer SAGE survey) and studies of embedded clusters in more distant galaxies using JWST's superior resolution and sensitivity at mid-infrared wavelengths, thereby enabling systematic identification and characterization of dusty young stellar populations beyond the Local Group.
AI.method: JWST NIRCam (2, 4 μm) and MIRI (10, 21 μm) imaging of four galaxies at 1-5 Mpc; color-magnitude selection criteria (F1000W vs. F1000W-F2100W) defined using SAGE-LMC catalog guidance; resolution-degradation experiments to test selection stability; luminosity function analysis; comparison with PAH-selected young clusters from PHANGS.
AI.result: Identified 216, 32, 80, and 139 dusty young objects across M33, NGC300, NGC7793, and NGC5068 respectively. Color selection stable across 1-5 Mpc; 10 μm luminosity function slope α ~ -2. Blending causes ~50% incompleteness at 5.2 Mpc, biasing toward brighter sources (F1000W < 19 mag). Stellar masses ~10-2×10⁵ M⊙. ~80% recovery of PAH-selected clusters in NGC5068. Practical limit for individual MYSO study is ~3 Mpc.
AI.conclusion: JWST enables systematic identification of embedded young stellar populations in galaxies beyond the Magellanic Clouds, but spatial resolution imposes fundamental limits: individual MYSOs are distinguishable only within ~3 Mpc, beyond which blending and surface-brightness dilution introduce incompleteness and biases toward brighter objects. The catalog provides a foundation for resolved studies of star formation rates and early cluster evolution.

title: PSZ: The meta-catalogue of Planck Sunyaev-Zeldovich sources
comment: 20 pages + Appendix (12 pages), 36 figures, submitted to A&A
summary: We present the PSZ, a meta-catalogue of 1962 clusters and cluster candidates produced by the Planck Collaboration. The PSZ contains fully-updated validation information for all official Planck catalogue detections, together with redshift estimates for confirmed clusters, with no duplicate entries. The validation is derived from optical and X-ray follow-up campaigns, supplemented by cross-matching with external catalogues with redshift information, and with XMM-Newton archive data. The external catalogues considered include the all-sky X-ray catalogue MCXC-II, the eROSITA X-ray cluster catalogue, the RASS-MCMF and PSZ-MCMF catalogues, and the extended Planck catalogues of Burenin. A total of 281 clusters are newly-confirmed owing to this process; conversely, 262 Planck candidates are invalidated. Of the 1500 confirmed clusters, 274 have updated redshifts, and 278 have newly-assigned redshifts. An MCXC-II counterpart is assigned to 631 clusters, updating the MCXC cross-match published in the Planck catalogues. Differences with the PSZ2 update of Bahk & Hwang are discussed. We further introduce a new, homogeneously-derived mass estimate, corrected for selection effects owing to intrinsic scatter and the properties of the underlying mass function. New posterior probability contours in the $Y_{5R500}-θ_s$ plane are provided for all sources, in addition to the corresponding $M_{500}(z)$ degeneracy curves. PSZ includes both corrected and uncorrected $M_{500}$ values for confirmed clusters. A methodology for cross-identification between catalogues is presented. We show that simple fixed-distance matching is insufficient for this task, and demonstrate the need for additional consistency checks based on mass proxies, redshifts, and distance versus angular size comparisons. The final PSZ comprises 1500 confirmed clusters, 262 noise-dominated detections, and 200 candidates awaiting validation.

AI.tldr: PSZ is a meta-catalogue of 1962 Planck clusters, validated via optical/X-ray follow-up, with 1500 confirmed, 262 invalidated, and 200 pending; includes homogeneous mass estimates, redshift updates, and cross-identification methodology.
AI.motivation: To provide a unified, fully-updated validation of all Planck cluster candidates, eliminating duplicates and incorporating new confirmations, redshift assignments, and mass estimates with selection-effect corrections.
AI.method: Validation via optical/X-ray follow-up campaigns, cross-matching with external catalogues (MCXC-II, eROSITA, RASS-MCMF, PSZ-MCMF, Burenin), XMM-Newton archive data, and a new cross-identification methodology requiring consistency checks beyond fixed-distance matching. Homogeneous mass estimates corrected for intrinsic scatter and mass function selection.
AI.result: 1962 entries: 1500 confirmed clusters (274 updated redshifts, 278 newly assigned), 262 invalidated, 200 pending. 281 newly confirmed. 631 clusters assigned MCXC-II counterparts. Posterior probability contours in Y5R500–θs plane and M500(z) degeneracy curves provided.
AI.conclusion: Simple fixed-distance matching is insufficient for cross-identification; additional consistency checks based on mass proxies, redshifts, and distance–angular size relations are necessary. PSZ offers a homogeneous, selection-corrected mass estimate and a clean, non-redundant catalogue.

title: Dust in the Average Galaxy: Attenuation, Emission, and Opacity from 0<z<7
comment: 50 pages, 21 figures; submitted to OJA. Table 1 provides measured empirical relations. Data tables available at https://github.com/caitlinmcasey/duststacks
summary: We present constraints on the dust emission and attenuation properties of galaxies across 0<z<7 using JWST imaging from the COSMOS-Web Survey combined with deep FIR/(sub)millimeter data from Spitzer, Herschel, SCUBA-2, NIKA-2 and ALMA. We analyze over 500,000 galaxies to independently constrain attenuation in the rest-frame UV/optical as well as dust emission from stacked FIR SEDs, enabling a direct comparison between the two. We find UV/optical attenuation systematically underpredicts IR luminosity by a factor of ~3x at 0.5<z<7 and up to an order of magnitude for $M_\star>10^{10.5}M_\odot$. We derive empirical relationships for the effective attenuation, dust temperature, fraction of star formation that is unobscured, and dust-to-stellar mass ratio as functions of redshift and stellar mass. We separate the first order effect of star/dust geometry from dust grain properties by combining constraints on the IR SED, UV SED, and dust mass surface density. Importantly, we measure over an order of magnitude decrease in $κ_{UV}/κ_{FIR}$--the ratio of dust mass absorption coefficients in the UV at 1600Å and FIR at 500$μ$m--from z~0 to z~7. A depressed $κ_{UV}/κ_{FIR}$ is consistent with a deficit of small dust grains, possibly attributable to the intense radiation fields of high-$z$ star formation; indeed, we find a redshift-invariant inverse relationship between $κ_{UV}/κ_{FIR}$ and $Σ_{SFR}$. Most evolution in the dust-to-stellar ratio is at $z<1$, the product of mild downward evolution in the dust-to-gas ratio combined with steep evolution in the gas-to-stellar ratio. The significant evolution and dynamic range of $κ_{UV}/κ_{FIR}$ and prevailing disconnect between the UV/optical and FIR regimes emphasize that direct dust constraints are irreplaceable for the majority of star-forming galaxies at z<7, not just the most extreme star-formers.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes dust emission and attenuation properties of over 500,000 galaxies across 0<z<7 using JWST COSMOS-Web survey combined with FIR/submillimeter data. It finds that UV/optical attenuation systematically underpredicts IR luminosity by ~3x (up to 10x for massive galaxies), and measures over an order of magnitude decrease in the UV-to-FIR dust absorption coefficient ratio (κ_UV/κ_FIR) from z~0 to z~7, consistent with a deficit of small dust grains at high redshift driven by intense star formation.
AI.motivation: To provide direct, empirical constraints on dust emission and attenuation across a wide redshift range (0<z<7) using a large sample of galaxies, and to understand the disconnect between UV/optical attenuation and FIR emission, which has significant implications for galaxy evolution studies.
AI.method: The study uses JWST imaging from the COSMOS-Web Survey combined with deep FIR/submillimeter data from Spitzer, Herschel, SCUBA-2, NIKA-2, and ALMA. Over 500,000 galaxies are analyzed, with independent constraints on rest-frame UV/optical attenuation and dust emission from stacked FIR SEDs. Empirical relationships are derived for effective attenuation, dust temperature, unobscured SF fraction, and dust-to-stellar mass ratio as functions of redshift and stellar mass.
AI.result: (1) UV/optical attenuation systematically underpredicts IR luminosity by ~3x at 0.5<z<7, up to 10x for M_*>10^10.5 M_sun. (2) Over an order of magnitude decrease in κ_UV/κ_FIR from z~0 to z~7, indicating a deficit of small dust grains at high redshift. (3) A redshift-invariant inverse relationship between κ_UV/κ_FIR and Σ_SFR. (4) Most evolution in dust-to-stellar ratio occurs at z<1, driven by mild evolution in dust-to-gas ratio combined with steep evolution in gas-to-stellar ratio.
AI.conclusion: Direct dust constraints are irreplaceable for the majority of star-forming galaxies at z<7, not just extreme star-formers, due to the significant evolution and dynamic range of κ_UV/κ_FIR and the prevailing disconnect between UV/optical and FIR regimes.

title: A rare sextuple-merging brightest cluster galaxy system in a disturbed galaxy cluster observed with the Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope
comment: 7 pages, 6 figures. Accepted for publication in A&A
summary: The evolutionary processes of galaxy clusters influence the properties of their member galaxies. We present a joint X-ray--optical analysis of the galaxy cluster WHY J050106.2+013714 at $z_{\rm c}=0.151$. X-ray observations with the Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope indicate that the cluster is dynamically young. The cluster displays an average X-ray temperature of $2.8^{+0.4}_{-0.3}$ keV and a total luminosity of 9.4$\pm0.3\times10^{43}$ erg s$^{-1}$, consistent with the scaling relation of typical disturbed clusters. Remarkably, the cluster hosts a multi-merging brightest cluster galaxy (BCG) system composed of six massive galaxies, with a total stellar mass of $1.16\times10^{12}M_{\odot}$. We detected a well-defined intracluster light component extending to a size of 310 kpc. A systematic search for merging BCGs in the DESI Legacy Surveys reveals that this sextuple-merging BCG is extremely rare in the local Universe. Additionally, other merging BCGs are also likely to form in moderately disturbed clusters, which provides valuable insights into the formation of BCGs.

AI.tldr: This paper analyzes the dynamically young galaxy cluster WHY J050106.2+013714 at z=0.151 using joint X-ray and optical observations, finding it hosts an extremely rare sextuple-merging BCG system and providing insights into BCG formation in moderately disturbed clusters.
AI.motivation: To understand how evolutionary processes of galaxy clusters influence the properties of their member galaxies, particularly through studying a rare multi-merging BCG system.
AI.method: Joint X-ray--optical analysis using Einstein Probe Follow-up X-ray Telescope for X-ray observations and DESI Legacy Surveys for systematic search of merging BCGs.
AI.result: The cluster is dynamically young with X-ray temperature 2.8^{+0.4}_{-0.3} keV and luminosity 9.4±0.3×10^43 erg s^{-1}. It hosts a sextuple-merging BCG system with total stellar mass 1.16×10^12 M⊙ and an intracluster light component spanning 310 kpc. Such sextuple-merging BCGs are extremely rare in the local Universe.
AI.conclusion: Merging BCGs are likely to form in moderately disturbed clusters, providing valuable insights into the formation pathways of brightest cluster galaxies.

title: Black Hole Stars Across the Universe: Identifying Central Engine Dominated Little Red Dots at $z\sim1.5-9.5$
comment: 37 pages, 27 figures, to be submitted to OJAp, catalog of BH*-dominated LRDs available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20611334, we encourage community follow-up
summary: Photometric selections of Little Red Dots (LRDs) largely rely on identifying their ``V-shaped'' spectral energy distribution (SED). Recent work suggests this V-shape stems from a combination of a central engine -- also referred to as a Black Hole Star (BH*) -- and a star-forming host galaxy. We present a new and highly complementary photometric selection that is based on incorporating BH* templates in the \texttt{eazy} redshift fitting code. Selecting compact sources where a BH* template contributes $>80$\% to the best fitting SED in the rest-optical, we compile a sample of 241 BH*-dominated candidates from $\sim1000\,{\rm arcmin}^2$ of legacy and pure parallel JWST imaging. Our selection does not require a blue UV-component, and it successfully identifies objects that resemble the paradigmatic sources ``MoM-BH*-1'' and ``The Cliff''. We find that BH*-dominated sources exist across a wide range of redshifts ($z\sim1.7-9.3$) and optical luminosities (log$(L_{5100}/{\rm erg}\,{\rm s}^{-1})\sim42-44.5$), and we measure a median Balmer break strength of $\sim3$, with some breaks reaching values $>10$. We estimate bolometric luminosities in the range log$(L_{\rm bol}/{\rm erg}\,{\rm s}^{-1})\sim42-45$, which, assuming accretion at the Eddington-limit, would translate to black hole masses of $M_{\rm BH}\sim10^4-10^7{\rm M_\odot}$, spanning the intermediate mass black hole to the quasar regime. The number density of BH*-dominated candidates peaks at $z\sim5-6$ ($\sim10^{-5}\,{\rm Mpc}^{-3}$) and it declines by an order of magnitude down to $z\sim2$. Tentatively, comparing to V-shaped LRD samples suggests that the fraction of BH*-dominated sources among the broader LRD population does not decrease towards lower redshift. Crucially, our work demonstrates that BH*-dominated sources are not merely an early-Universe phenomenon but rather persist at least until cosmic noon.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a new photometric selection method for Little Red Dots (LRDs) that uses Black Hole Star (BH*) templates in the eazy redshift fitting code, identifying 241 BH*-dominated candidates across JWST imaging. These sources span redshifts z~1.7-9.3, have Balmer breaks ~3, and bolometric luminosities ~10^42-10^45 erg/s, implying black hole masses of 10^4-10^7 M⊙. Their number density peaks at z~5-6 and declines by an order of magnitude by z~2, showing BH*-dominated sources persist until cosmic noon.
AI.motivation: Traditional V-shaped SED selection of LRDs may miss objects lacking a strong blue UV component. The authors aim to develop a complementary selection method incorporating BH* templates to more robustly identify BH*-dominated sources and study their properties across cosmic time.
AI.method: The authors incorporate BH* templates into the eazy photometric redshift fitting code. They select compact sources where a BH* template contributes >80% to the best-fitting SED in the rest-optical. The selection is applied to ~1000 arcmin² of legacy and pure parallel JWST imaging, yielding 241 candidates.
AI.result: BH*-dominated sources are found at z~1.7-9.3 with optical luminosities log(L_5100)~42-44.5 erg/s. Median Balmer break strength ~3 (some >10). Bolometric luminosities log(L_bol)~42-45 erg/s imply M_BH~10^4-10^7 M⊙. Number density peaks at z~5-6 (~10^-5 Mpc^-3), declining 10× by z~2. The fraction of BH*-dominated sources among broader LRDs does not decrease at lower redshift.
AI.conclusion: BH*-dominated sources are not exclusively an early-Universe phenomenon; they persist at least until cosmic noon (z~2). The new selection method complements V-shaped SED approaches and reveals a population of intermediate-mass to quasar-scale black holes across a wide redshift range.

title: Alleviating the Hubble tension with the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM model
comment: Proceeding AstroMarche2 conference, September 2025, Accepted for publication in IJMPA, 7 pages, 2 figures, 1 table
summary: We formulate a novel extension of the $Λ$CDM model, named $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM, in which we consider an additional term at early times in order to alleviate the Hubble tension. This additional component, referred to as \emph{matter with pressure}, indicates a barotropic fluid that is subdominant to dust and radiation as the Universe expands, thereby recovering the $Λ$CDM paradigm at late times. We constrain the $Λ_{ω_s}$CDM cosmology by performing a Markov Chain Monte Carlo analysis with Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2, and Pantheon+\texttt{SH0ES} data. The results suggest that the barotropic factor and the normalized density of the new fluid are given, respectively, by $ω_s=0.294_{-0.004(0.023)}^{+0.014(0.015)}$ and $10^{5}Ω_s=1.62_{-0.56(0.91)}^{+0.36(1.02)}$. With these two additional parameters, the Hubble constant is increased to $H_0 = 71.51^{+0.72(1.43)}_{-0.74(1.46)}$ km/s/Mpc, alleviating \emph{de facto} the Hubble tension.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a Λ_ω_sCDM extension of ΛCDM with an early-time barotropic fluid to resolve the Hubble tension. MCMC analysis with Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2, and Pantheon+SH0ES data yields ω_s=0.294 and Ω_s~1.62×10⁻⁵, raising H₀ to 71.51 km/s/Mpc, effectively alleviating the Hubble tension.
AI.motivation: To alleviate the Hubble tension by extending ΛCDM with an additional early-time matter-with-pressure component that is subdominant at late times.
AI.method: A Λ_ω_sCDM model is formulated with a barotropic fluid (equation-of-state parameter ω_s) added at early times. The model is constrained via MCMC analysis using Planck 2018 CMB, DESI DR2, and Pantheon+SH0ES data.
AI.result: The barotropic factor ω_s = 0.294 and normalized density 10⁵Ω_s = 1.62. The Hubble constant is inferred as H₀ = 71.51 km/s/Mpc, which substantially reduces the Hubble tension.
AI.conclusion: The Λ_ω_sCDM model effectively alleviates the Hubble tension with two extra parameters, recovering ΛCDM behavior at late times while raising H₀ to a value consistent with local measurements.

title: Reduced Effective Viscosity from Anisotropic Transport and Plasma Instabilities in the Sloshing Cores of Galaxy Clusters
comment: 30 pages, 18 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: The $\sim μ$G magnetic field in the intracluster medium (ICM) introduces a pressure anisotropy with respect to the magnetic field's direction that manifests as an anisotropic viscous stress. Plasma instabilities arising from the pressure anisotropy crossing certain thresholds force it to marginally stable values, reducing viscous transport. Additionally, the feedback of this anisotropic pressure on the velocity field has been predicted to lead to a form of self-organization that also can reduce viscous dissipation without affecting the collisionality. In this work, we present high-resolution Braginskii-MHD simulations of a galaxy cluster core with sloshing gas motions and turbulence, including the effects of anisotropic viscous stress and different simple prescriptions for limiting the pressure anisotropy due to plasma instabilities. Braginskii viscosity has an expected, though modest, effect on suppressing Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities at sloshing cold front surfaces, dependent on how the pressure anisotropy is limited. Due to the sloshing motions, the magnetic field's strength can become high enough in places that the pressure anisotropy need not be limited. Nevertheless, the combined effect of the limiters and the turbulent structure of the magnetic field in all simulations is that the effective viscosity is much lower than the isotropic Spitzer value in a significant fraction of the core region. However, we find that this reduced viscosity is capable of steepening the velocity-amplitude spectrum and transferring a small fraction of the turbulent kinetic energy into heat. Finally, we present evidence for magneto-immutable dynamics in our simulations.

AI.tldr: Braginskii-MHD simulations show that pressure anisotropy from ICM magnetic fields reduces effective viscosity below Spitzer values in galaxy cluster cores, but the residual viscosity still steepens velocity spectra and dissipates turbulent kinetic energy, with evidence for magneto-immutable dynamics.
AI.motivation: To understand how plasma instabilities limiting pressure anisotropy in the weakly collisional ICM affect viscous transport, turbulent dissipation, and dynamics of sloshing gas motions in galaxy cluster cores.
AI.method: High-resolution Braginskii-MHD simulations of a galaxy cluster core with sloshing motions and turbulence, incorporating anisotropic viscous stress and prescriptions for limiting pressure anisotropy due to plasma instabilities.
AI.result: Braginskii viscosity modestly suppresses Kelvin-Helmholtz instabilities at sloshing cold fronts; effective viscosity is much lower than isotropic Spitzer value in a significant fraction of the core; the reduced viscosity still steepens the velocity-amplitude spectrum and transfers a small fraction of turbulent kinetic energy into heat; evidence for magneto-immutable dynamics is found.
AI.conclusion: Pressure anisotropy limiters and turbulent magnetic field structure combine to significantly reduce effective viscosity in the ICM, but the residual viscosity remains dynamically important for turbulence dissipation and spectral steepening, and magneto-immutable self-organization occurs.

title: Two-population model of type Ia supernovae and their associations with host galaxies in ZTF DR2
comment: to be submitted to A&A; 14 pages, 7 figures, 1 table
summary: We constrain type Ia supernova intrinsic properties, extinction, and probabilistic supernova-host associations using the volume-limited sample from the Zwicky Transient Factory DR2, the largest selection-free data set of type Ia supernovae to date. We employ Bayesian hierarchical modelling to jointly analyse the distribution of SALT2 light-curve parameters and global host-galaxy properties (stellar mass and rest-frame g-z colour). The adopted model is a mixture of distributions representing two supernova populations corresponding to two distinct modes of the stretch-parameter distribution, and two host-galaxy populations corresponding to two modes in the host-galaxy parameter space (red/massive and blue/less massive). Motivated by observations, high-stretch supernovae are allowed to populate both host-galaxy populations, whereas low-stretch supernovae are assumed to be exclusively associated with the red/massive host-galaxy population. The apparent non-linearity of the supernova magnitude-stretch relation implies a luminosity gap between the supernova populations, with the low-stretch population being Delta MB=0.14+/-0.03 mag brighter at x1=0, and different slopes (Delta alpha=0.064+/-0.023, steeper for the low-stretch population). The mean extinction coefficient is RB=3.89+/-0.29 (consistent with typical Milky Way values) in the blue/less massive host-galaxy population, which contains 68 per cent of high-stretch supernovae, and RB=3.08+/-0.08 in the red/massive host-galaxy population. Host-galaxy step corrections, both in stellar mass and colour, naturally emerge from the way the two supernova populations, characterised by different intrinsic luminosities and exctinctions, are distributed across host-galaxy populations. The adopted framework for modelling supernova populations and supernova-host associations makes host-galaxy step corrections redundant.

AI.tldr: This paper uses Bayesian hierarchical modeling to analyze type Ia supernovae from ZTF DR2, revealing two distinct supernova populations with different intrinsic properties, extinction laws, and host-galaxy associations, making traditional host-galaxy step corrections unnecessary.
AI.motivation: To constrain type Ia supernova intrinsic properties, extinction, and probabilistic supernova-host associations using a large, selection-free dataset to better understand population heterogeneity and its impact on cosmological analyses.
AI.method: Bayesian hierarchical modeling applied to SALT2 light-curve parameters and host-galaxy properties (stellar mass, rest-frame g-z color), using a mixture model with two supernova populations (high/low stretch) and two host-galaxy populations (red/massive and blue/less massive), with constraints on associations between populations.
AI.result: Low-stretch SNe are ΔMB=0.14±0.03 mag brighter at x1=0 with steeper magnitude-stretch slope (Δα=0.064±0.023). Extinction coefficient RB differs: 3.89±0.29 (blue hosts, 68% high-stretch SNe) vs 3.08±0.08 (red hosts). Host-galaxy step corrections emerge naturally from population distributions.
AI.conclusion: The joint modeling of supernova populations and host associations renders traditional host-galaxy step corrections redundant, as the observed steps arise from the differential distribution of intrinsically different SN populations across host types.

title: The Incidence of Large Ionized Bubbles at Redshift 13
comment: 19 pages, 8 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary: Ionized bubbles around the first galaxies link early galaxy growth, ionizing photon escape, intergalactic-medium topology, Lyα visibility, 21 cm structure, and the timing of reionization. With JWST now constraining both the abundance of luminous galaxies at $z\gtrsim 10$ and rare Ly$α$ emitters deep in the neutral era, it is timely to ask how often galaxy populations produce large ionized environments. We model the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at $z\approx 13$ using JWST UV luminosity functions, taking the Ly$α$ source reported by Witstok et al. (2025) as a benchmark for the relevant bubble scale. We quantify the incidence of regions with comoving radius $R\ge 2.5$ cMpc through the sky surface density $Σ_{\ge 2.5}$ at $z\approx 13$. For our fiducial case (UVLF from Donnan et al. 2024 with $f_{\mathrm{esc}}=0.2$, $\logξ_{\mathrm{ion}}=25.5$, $f_{\mathrm{duty}}=1$, and $C=3$), we find $Σ_{\ge 2.5}\simeq 1.33\times 10^{-2}$ arcmin$^{-2}$ per $Δz=1$. Because bubbles are treated as independent spheres with random source positions and no union of overlaps, this is a conservative baseline for the abundance of connected ionized environments. We conclude that Witstok-sized regions are plausible in UVLF-calibrated galaxy-driven models. This is a population-level statement, however, and the specific Witstok source may still require unusual effective ionizing efficiency, recent fading or burstiness, or a non-stellar ionizing contribution.

AI.tldr: This paper models the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at z≈13 using JWST UV luminosity functions, finding that large bubbles (≥2.5 cMpc radius) are plausible in standard galaxy-driven reionization models, with a sky surface density of ~1.33×10⁻² arcmin⁻² per Δz=1, though the specific Witstok et al. (2025) Lyα source may still require unusual ionizing properties.
AI.motivation: To understand how often galaxy populations produce large ionized environments at z≈13, motivated by JWST constraints on luminous galaxies and rare Lyα emitters in the neutral era, using the Witstok et al. (2025) Lyα source as a benchmark bubble scale.
AI.method: Modeling the incidence of galaxy-driven ionized bubbles at z≈13 using JWST UV luminosity functions (Donnan et al. 2024), with parameters f_esc=0.2, log ξ_ion=25.5, f_duty=1, C=3. Bubbles are treated as independent spheres with random source positions and no union of overlaps, providing a conservative baseline.
AI.result: The sky surface density of regions with comoving radius R≥2.5 cMpc at z≈13 is Σ_≥2.5 ≈ 1.33×10⁻² arcmin⁻² per Δz=1, indicating that Witstok-sized bubbles are plausible in UVLF-calibrated galaxy-driven models.
AI.conclusion: Witstok-sized ionized regions are plausible under standard galaxy-driven reionization models at the population level, though the specific Witstok source may still require unusual effective ionizing efficiency, recent fading/burstiness, or a non-stellar ionizing contribution.

title: Data-Driven Discovery of a Simple Phantom-Crossing Dark Energy Parametrization
comment: 30 pages, 7 figures, 3 tables. Comments welcome!
summary: We develop a data-driven reconstruction programme for the dark-energy equation of state within VCDM, a minimally modified gravity framework in which both background and linear perturbations can be consistently evolved across the phantom divide. Using CMB, BAO, and type-Ia supernova data, we first perform a Bayesian spline reconstruction of $w(a)$, finding a preference for smooth, monotonic phantom-crossing trajectories. Bayesian evidence disfavors increasingly complex spline models, indicating that current observations exhibit a statistical preference for low-complexity dark-energy dynamics. Motivated by this result, we apply Exhaustive Symbolic Regression, an interpretable machine-learning technique that systematically searches over analytic expressions of fixed complexity, identifying the remarkably simple one-parameter form $w(a)={w_0}/{\sqrt a}$, which reproduces the reconstructed behaviour and fits the data at a level comparable to standard two-parameter parametrizations such as CPL. The model naturally crosses the phantom divide for $w_0<0$, suppresses early dark energy, and predicts a transient accelerating and phantom phase without a future big-rip singularity. As a one-parameter model, it is highly predictive, being a genuinely dynamical deformation of the cosmological constant rather than containing it as a limit. Bayesian model comparison yields mild-to-moderate support for this parametrization relative to standard two-parameter alternatives, and stronger evidence relative to $Λ$CDM. Our results suggest that current observations favour surprisingly simple dark-energy dynamics and illustrate how Bayesian reconstruction and symbolic regression can be combined into a principled model-discovery framework for cosmology.

AI.tldr: The authors combine Bayesian spline reconstruction and symbolic regression on CMB, BAO, and supernova data to find that dark-energy dynamics is surprisingly simple: a one-parameter model $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$ that crosses the phantom divide, suppresses early dark energy, avoids big-rip singularities, and is mildly-to-moderately favored over two-parameter alternatives and more strongly favored over $\Lambda$CDM.
AI.motivation: To develop a data-driven, minimally-assumed reconstruction of the dark-energy equation of state within VCDM (a modified gravity framework that consistently handles phantom-crossing) and to discover interpretable, low-complexity analytic forms that best describe current cosmological observations.
AI.method: The authors use (i) Bayesian spline reconstruction with increasing complexity to map $w(a)$ from CMB, BAO, and SNIa data, (ii) Bayesian evidence to penalize overfitting, and (iii) Exhaustive Symbolic Regression to systematically search over analytic expressions of fixed complexity, identifying the best one-parameter form.
AI.result: The optimal model is $w(a)=w_0/\sqrt{a}$, a one-parameter form that naturally crosses the phantom divide (for $w_0<0$), suppresses early dark energy, and yields a transient accelerating/phantom phase with no big-rip. It fits data comparably to CPL (two-parameter) and receives mild-to-moderate Bayesian evidence relative to two-parameter alternatives and stronger evidence relative to $\Lambda$CDM.
AI.conclusion: Current cosmological data favor surprisingly simple dark-energy dynamics, and the combination of Bayesian reconstruction with symbolic regression provides a principled model-discovery framework that can identify predictive, physically meaningful parametrizations beyond the cosmological constant.

title: OQ~208: A New Fe~II Changing-look Active Galactic Nucleus and Implications for the Nature of the Changing-look Phenomenon
comment: 12 pages, 6 figures and 2 tables, accepted by ApJ
summary: In addition to the traditional hydrogen Balmer emission lines, here we extend the optical changing-look (CL) phenomenon occurring in some active galactic nuclei (AGNs) to the optical FeII complex. Multiepoch spectroscopy allows to identify OQ~208, a local flat-spectrum radio source, as a new FeII CL-AGN owing to the disappearance of both its strong FeII complex (RFe $\equiv$ FeII/H$β=0.64$) and its Balmer broad-line emission on a timescale of $\sim14$\,yr. The simultaneous disappearance implies that in this object, both the FeII and Balmer emission come from the same region exposed to the ionizing continuum. We further identify an anticorrelation between the FeII strength and the continuum (and also Eddington ratio) during the CL events in dozens of CL-AGNs recently studied by Panda \& Sniegowska (2024), suggesting a negative response of RFe to both $L_{5100}$ and $L_{\mathrm{bol}}/L_{\mathrm{Edd}}$; this can be understood by the Comptonization process in a hot, optically thin accretion flow.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the changing-look phenomenon in AGNs from Balmer lines to optical FeII complex, identifying OQ~208 as a new FeII CL-AGN where FeII and Balmer emission disappeared simultaneously over ~14 years. It also finds an anticorrelation between FeII strength and continuum/Eddington ratio across dozens of CL-AGNs, explained by Comptonization in a hot, optically thin accretion flow.
AI.motivation: To demonstrate that the changing-look phenomenon in AGNs occurs not only in traditional Balmer lines but also in the optical FeII complex, and to understand the physical mechanism driving the variability of FeII emission.
AI.method: Multiepoch spectroscopy of OQ~208, a local flat-spectrum radio source, combined with a statistical analysis of dozens of CL-AGNs from Panda & Sniegowska (2024) to examine correlations between FeII strength, continuum luminosity at 5100 Å, and Eddington ratio.
AI.result: OQ~208 shows disappearance of both FeII complex (RFe = 0.64) and Balmer broad-line emission over ~14 years. An anticorrelation is found between FeII strength and both L_5100 and L_bol/L_Edd across CL-AGNs.
AI.conclusion: FeII and Balmer emission originate from the same region exposed to the ionizing continuum. The negative response of RFe to continuum and Eddington ratio can be explained by Comptonization in a hot, optically thin accretion flow.

title: Weak-lensing mass calibration of \emph{Planck} Sunyaev--Zel'dovich clusters with HSC-SSP Year~3
comment: 27 pages, 10 figures, submitted to PRD
summary: We present a weak gravitational lensing mass calibration of 19 \textit{Planck} Sunyaev--Zel'dovich (SZ) selected galaxy clusters using shape measurements from the Hyper Suprime-Cam Subaru Strategic Program (HSC-SSP) Year 3 shape catalog. We measure the stacked weak-lensing signal $ΔΣ(R)$ using per-cluster lensing weights that match the measurement pipeline's stacking scheme, and construct an analytical covariance matrix that includes shape noise and projected large-scale structure contributions. Our primary constraint on the SZ mass bias comes from a forward-modeling approach that integrates over the halo mass function while accounting for the \textit{Planck} SZ selection function, Eddington bias from log-normal scatter in the SZ mass proxy, and cluster miscentering. Fitting four free parameters, the log mass bias $\ln(1-b)$, the miscentered fraction $f_{\rm mis}$, the offset scale $σ_{\rm off}$, and the SZ scatter $σ_{\ln M}$, over the radial range $0.5$--$5.0\,h^{-1}\,\mathrm{Mpc}$, we obtain $1-b = 0.73^{+0.10}_{-0.11}$ with $χ^2/\mathrm{dof} = 5.2/5$ at an effective redshift $z_{\rm eff}\simeq 0.24$. This measurement is consistent with recent weak-lensing calibrations of SZ-selected clusters and supports the picture that significant mass bias corrections are required to reconcile cluster abundance measurements with primary cosmic microwave background constraints on cosmological parameters.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a weak gravitational lensing mass calibration of 19 Planck SZ-selected galaxy clusters using HSC-SSP Year 3 shape data, finding a mass bias factor of 1-b = 0.73^{+0.10}_{-0.11} that supports the need for significant bias corrections to reconcile cluster abundance with CMB cosmology.
